name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve
notes: Florida's first DarkSky park. The gate closes 15 minutes after sunset, so reserve a campsite or astronomy pad and check in with the ranger before dark; red lights only on the pads.

name: Hopkins Prairie
notes: Small Forest Service campground overlooking an open prairie, with vault toilets and no electricity. Come in from SR 19 via FR 86 and FR 111, since Google Maps' northern route doesn't work.

name: Lake Louisa State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving late must call 352-394-3969 for the gate code before closing.

name: Black Point Wildlife Drive
notes: Wide marsh views over the Indian River, but refuge roads are open sunrise to sunset only, so there is no night access.

name: Lake Eola Park
notes: City park that stays open until midnight. Good for the Moon, planets and bright satellite passes; the Milky Way is washed out.

name: Alexander Springs Recreation Area
notes: Forest Service campground beside the spring. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; day-use hours vary by season.

name: Juniper Springs Recreation Area
notes: Forest Service campground around the spring. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; the boardwalk is closed for renovation.

name: Silver Springs State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and the campground has its own entrance at 1425 NE 58th Ave. Campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset call 407-553-4383 for the gate combination. Day visitors need an entry reservation.

name: UCF Reflecting Pond
notes: Campus lawn by Millican Hall where UCF's Planetary Sciences Group has set up telescopes for Moon viewing; good for the Moon and planets, not the Milky Way. Visitors need an $8 virtual daily parking permit.

name: Moss Park
notes: County campground between Lake Hart and Lake Mary Jane. The park closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer, so after dark it's campers only.

name: Lake Apopka Wildlife Drive
notes: One-way 11-mile drive open to cars Friday to Sunday and federal holidays. The gate takes vehicles 7 AM to 3 PM and everyone must be out by 5 PM, so there is no night access.

name: Blue Spring State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset call 386-775-3663 for the gate combination. A camping reservation doubles as the entry reservation.

name: Playalinda Beach
notes: The seashore is open 6 AM to 6 PM under normal hours and closes for some rocket launches, so there is no night access.

name: Jetty Park
notes: The park closes at 9 PM except to campground guests, who keep beach access and 24-hour pier access. Campers can stay overnight to watch launches from the beach or pier.

name: Sebastian Inlet State Park
notes: Open 24 hours with a staffed north ranger station, so no campsite is needed. Use the north-side lots; south-side beach access is closed during bridge construction.

name: Three Lakes WMA, Prairie Lakes Unit
seasonalNote: No camping during Prairie Lakes quota hunts
notes: Primitive campsites by Lake Jackson need a free FWC camping permit, plus a daily-use permit to enter. Come in from CR 523 via Prairie Lakes Rd, since the route from SR 60 doesn't go through.

name: Colt Creek State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Withlacoochee River Park
notes: The St. Petersburg Astronomy Club's dark-sky site: astronomers camp on the open activity field on new-moon weekends, since the campground is shaded by oaks. The park is open dawn to dusk, so stay with a campsite.

name: Hillsborough River State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Salt Springs Recreation Area
notes: The largest campground in the Ocala National Forest, and the only one with full RV hookups. Gates close in the evening (8 PM in summer), so check in early; there's no cell service.

name: Clearwater Lake Campground
notes: 42-site Forest Service campground with lakefront sites. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; day use ends at 4 PM.

name: Holder Mine Campground
notes: Improved state forest campground with electric sites, reserved through ReserveAmerica. Busy with hunters during archery and small-game seasons.

name: Lake Griffin State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Kelly Park / Rock Springs
notes: County park that closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer. After hours the waterfront is closed and campers must stay in the campground.

name: Trimble Park
notes: Small county campground on a point between Lake Carlton and Lake Beauclair. The park closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer, so after dark it's campers only.

name: Bill Frederick Park at Turkey Lake
notes: City park with RV sites and cabins on Turkey Lake. It closes at 5 PM from November to March and 7 PM from April to October, so after dark it's overnight guests only; best for the Moon and planets.

name: Cranes Roost Park
notes: City lakefront park open until 11 PM (midnight on Friday and Saturday). It's brightly lit, so come for the Moon, planets and the brightest stars.

name: Daytona Beach at Main Street
notes: The beach is open to pedestrians 24 hours, tides permitting, but cars are allowed only by day, so park off the beach near the Main Street Pier. Keep lights off the sand, which confuse nesting sea turtles.

name: Lighthouse Point Park
notes: County inlet park that closes at 7:30 PM in October and November, 6 PM in winter and 9 PM in summer, always before true darkness, so there is no night access.

name: Manatee Hammock Campground
notes: County campground on the Indian River facing the Kennedy Space Center launch pads. The park is open dawn to dusk, and anyone who isn't a registered camper must leave by 10 PM.

name: Lake Kissimmee State Park
seasonalNote: Campgrounds closed for renovation since February 2026
notes: The park closes at sundown, and its campgrounds are closed for renovation with no reopening date, so there is no night access for now.

name: Fisheating Creek Campground
notes: Concession-run campground in the Fisheating Creek WMA with RV and primitive sites; camping permits come from Fisheating Creek Outpost. Busiest on weekends and in the cooler months.

name: Little Manatee River State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Fort De Soto Park Campground
notes: County campground near the mouth of Tampa Bay. The front gate is locked from 9 PM to 5:30 AM, and registered campers get the gate combination at check-in.

name: Railroad Park
notes: Downtown green space that stays open late. Fine for the Moon and planets, but city glow hides faint stars.

name: Oak Mountain State Park
notes: Alabama's largest state park, just south of the city. After dark it's campers only, so book a site.

name: Papago Park
notes: Red sandstone buttes between Phoenix and Tempe. Good for the Moon and planets over the desert.

name: Lost Dutchman State Park
notes: Campground at the foot of the Superstition Mountains, with a dark eastern sky. Campers only after the park closes.

name: Big Dam Bridge
notes: Pedestrian bridge over the Arkansas River, open 24 hours. Wide views, but strong city glow.

name: Pinnacle Mountain State Park
notes: Park west of town where the open lots by the Arkansas River give a clear western horizon.

name: Griffith Observatory
notes: Free public telescopes on most clear evenings. Too bright for the Milky Way, great for the Moon and planets.

name: Mount Pinos
seasonalNote: Road can close for snow in winter
notes: Southern California's classic astronomy site at 8,300 ft. Park at the Chula Vista lot and bring layers; it's cold at night.

name: Sloan's Lake
notes: City park on the west side of Denver. Bright, but good for the Moon and planets over the lake.

name: Echo Lake
seasonalNote: Mount Blue Sky Road above the lake closes for winter
notes: High lake at 10,600 ft on the Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway, a short drive up from Idaho Springs.

name: Elizabeth Park
notes: Rose garden park on the Hartford and West Hartford line. Fine for the Moon and bright planets.

name: Natchaug State Forest
notes: Quiet forest in Connecticut's darkest corner. The open fields near the horse camp give the widest sky.

name: Brandywine Creek State Park
notes: Rolling meadows just north of Wilmington. The hilltop fields give the widest sky.

name: Trap Pond State Park
notes: Bald cypress pond in rural southern Delaware with a campground, under some of the darkest skies in the state.

name: Piedmont Park
notes: Midtown park with the skyline as a backdrop. Good for the Moon and planets only.

name: Hard Labor Creek State Park
notes: Georgia State University's observatory sits inside the park, and campers can stay after dark.

name: Table Rock
notes: Mesa above Boise with big city views and a decent sky to the east.

name: Bruneau Dunes State Park
notes: The tallest single sand dune in North America, with a public observatory and weekend star programs in season.

name: Adler Planetarium Lakefront
notes: Lakefront next to the planetarium: dark water to the east, skyline glow everywhere else.

name: Starved Rock State Park
notes: Sandstone canyons on the Illinois River. Campers can stay after the park closes.

name: Holcomb Observatory
notes: Butler University's observatory, which holds public nights with its 38-inch telescope.

name: Brown County State Park
notes: Indiana's largest state park. Open ridgetop fields along the main road give big skies.

name: Gray's Lake Park
notes: Downtown lake with a lit pedestrian bridge. The Moon over the water is the draw.

name: Ledges State Park
notes: Sandstone bluffs on the Des Moines River with a campground. The upper lots have the best sky.

name: Riverside Park
notes: City park along the Little Arkansas River. Good for the Moon and planets.

name: Lake Afton Public Observatory
notes: Public observatory west of Wichita with weekend viewing nights.

name: Waterfront Park
notes: Riverfront lawns by the Big Four Bridge, with open views over the Ohio River.

name: Bernheim Forest
notes: Arboretum and forest south of town that closes at sunset, so there is no night access outside scheduled star events.

name: Lakeshore Drive
notes: Seawall steps along Lake Pontchartrain. The darkest sky is out over the lake to the north.

name: Fontainebleau State Park
notes: Lakefront park across the causeway in Mandeville. Campers can stay after the gate closes.

name: Fort Williams Park
notes: Next to Portland Head Light, with an ocean horizon to the east that is good for moonrise.

name: Sebago Lake State Park
notes: Big lake northwest of Portland with a campground and wide beach views.

name: Federal Hill Park
notes: Hilltop over the Inner Harbor. Skyline views and the Moon, little else.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park
notes: River valley park west of the city. The Hilltop area campground gives the best sky.

name: Castle Island
notes: Harbor point in South Boston with a low eastern horizon over the water.

name: Wompatuck State Park
notes: Wooded park south of Boston with a campground, and the darkest sky this close to the city.

name: Belle Isle Park
notes: Island park in the Detroit River. The open fields at the east end are the darkest.

name: Lake Hudson Recreation Area
notes: Michigan's first state dark sky preserve, open 24 hours with a lakeside field for telescopes.

name: Lake Harriet
notes: City lake with a bandshell and a walking path. Good for the Moon over the water.

name: Afton State Park
notes: Bluffs over the St. Croix River with hike-in campsites. The prairie hilltops give an open sky.

name: LeFleur's Bluff State Park
notes: In-city state park with a campground along the Pearl River.

name: Roosevelt State Park
notes: Lakeside park east of Jackson near Morton, with a campground and cabins.

name: Art Hill, Forest Park
notes: Grand lawn below the Art Museum, where the local astronomy society holds free public nights.

name: Cuivre River State Park
notes: Rugged wooded park north of the city. Campers can stay after dark.

name: Zimmerman Park
notes: Clifftop park on the Rimrocks above Billings: city lights below, dark sky above.

name: Bighorn Canyon NRA
notes: Remote canyon country south of Billings. The Barry's Landing area has near-pristine skies.

name: Chalco Hills Recreation Area
notes: Reservoir park on Omaha's southwest edge with an open view over the water.

name: Platte River State Park
notes: Wooded park between Omaha and Lincoln with cabins and a lookout tower.

name: Red Rock Canyon
notes: The scenic loop closes in the evening, so there is no night access.

name: Lee Canyon
seasonalNote: Ski traffic and snow in winter
notes: High in the Spring Mountains at 8,500 ft, an hour from the Strip. The Las Vegas glow sits low in the southeast.

name: Rock Rimmon Park
notes: Rock ledge park in west Manchester with a view over the city.

name: Bear Brook State Park
notes: Big forest park east of Manchester with a campground and open fields.

name: Liberty State Park
notes: Hudson River waterfront facing Lower Manhattan. The Moon and planets with a skyline view.

name: Jenny Jump State Forest
notes: Home of an amateur astronomy club's observatory, with public programs on Saturdays from spring to fall.

name: Petroglyph National Monument
notes: Trails close in the late afternoon, so there is no night access.

name: Sandia Crest
seasonalNote: Crest Highway can close for snow
notes: A 10,678 ft summit overlooking Albuquerque. The lot is at the end of NM 536.

name: Central Park Great Lawn
notes: Local astronomers set up telescopes here on clear nights. The park is open until 1 AM.

name: Harriman State Park
notes: Big forested park an hour north of the city. The lakeside lots have the most open sky.

name: Freedom Park
notes: Lakeside city park in Myers Park. Fine for the Moon and planets.

name: Morrow Mountain State Park
notes: Campground and overlooks in the Uwharrie Mountains, about an hour east of Charlotte.

name: Lindenwood Park
notes: Riverside park with campsites on Fargo's south side.

name: Sheyenne National Grassland
notes: Open tallgrass prairie southwest of Fargo with no lights to the horizon. Dispersed camping is allowed.

name: Scioto Mile
notes: Downtown riverfront promenade. The Moon over the river and the skyline.

name: John Glenn Astronomy Park
notes: Observatory plaza in Hocking Hills State Park with free public programs on clear weekend nights.

name: Scissortail Park
notes: Downtown park with a lake and wide lawns. Good for the Moon and planets.

name: Lake Thunderbird State Park
notes: Reservoir park east of Norman with campgrounds and open lakefront views.

name: Mount Tabor Park
notes: Volcanic cinder cone park in southeast Portland. The summit looks out over the whole city.

name: Milo McIver State Park
notes: Riverside park where local astronomers hold star parties. Campers can stay after dark.

name: Belmont Plateau
notes: Fairmount Park hilltop with a famous skyline view.

name: French Creek State Park
notes: Wooded park near Hopewell Furnace with two lakes and a campground.

name: Prospect Terrace Park
notes: Small College Hill overlook with a view west over downtown.

name: Frosty Drew Observatory
notes: Public observatory in Ninigret Park, Charlestown, open on clear Friday nights.

name: Riverfront Park
notes: Canal-side trail along the Congaree River downtown.

name: Congaree National Park
notes: Old-growth floodplain forest southeast of Columbia. The park is open 24 hours and runs night sky programs.

name: Falls Park
notes: Lit waterfalls downtown. Good for the Moon and planets only.

name: Newton Hills State Park
notes: Wooded hills south of Sioux Falls with a campground and open hilltop meadows.

name: Centennial Park
notes: Home of the Parthenon replica. The Moon over the lawn makes a good photo.

name: Long Hunter State Park
notes: Park on Percy Priest Lake east of Nashville with open lakefront fields.

name: Buffalo Bayou Park
notes: Downtown bayou park with skyline views. Good for the Moon and planets.

name: George Observatory
notes: Observatory in Brazos Bend State Park with public Saturday nights and a 36-inch telescope.

name: Liberty Park
notes: Central city park. Bright, but fine for the Moon and planets.

name: Antelope Island State Park
notes: Island in the Great Salt Lake and a DarkSky park. Buffalo Point and the campgrounds have an open western sky.

name: Waterfront Park
notes: Lake Champlain shoreline. The darkest sky is west over the lake toward the Adirondacks.

name: Little River State Park
notes: Campground by Waterbury Reservoir in the Green Mountains.

name: Belle Isle
notes: James River island reached by a footbridge. The river gives a low, open horizon.

name: Pocahontas State Park
notes: Virginia's largest state park, south of Richmond, with a campground and open lakeside fields.

name: Kerry Park
notes: Queen Anne viewpoint over the skyline and Mount Rainier. Good for the Moon and planets.

name: Rattlesnake Lake
notes: Lake below Rattlesnake Ledge, 45 minutes east of Seattle. The lot has an open view east.

name: Haddad Riverfront Park
notes: Kanawha River amphitheater downtown. Good for the Moon and planets.

name: Kanawha State Forest
notes: Forested hollows just south of Charleston with a campground.

name: Lakeshore State Park
notes: Urban park on Lake Michigan with a dark eastern horizon over the water.

name: Kettle Moraine Northern Unit
notes: Glacial hills an hour north of Milwaukee. The Mauthe Lake campground has an open sky.

name: Lions Park
notes: City park with a lake and the botanic gardens. Good for the Moon and planets.

name: Curt Gowdy State Park
notes: Granite hills and reservoirs halfway to Laramie, with campgrounds and a wide sky.
